sentences.zh: __FORCETOC__侯君集侯君集，豳州三水人。

translations.literal: __FORCETOC__Hou Junji — Hou Junji, a native of Sanshui in Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: __FORCETOC__Hou Junji was a native of Sanshui in Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以材雄稱。

translations.literal: He was famed for martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: He was renowned for his martial prowess.

sentences.zh: 少事秦王幕府，從征討有功，擢累左虞候、車騎將軍，封全椒縣子。

translations.literal: In youth he served in the Prince of Qin's staff; following campaigns and punitive expeditions he had merit, was promoted through Left Armor Guard and Cavalry General, and enfeoffed as heir of Quanjiao County.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served on the staff of the Prince of Qin; he followed him on campaigns and distinguished himself, rising through the posts of Left Armor Guard and Cavalry General and receiving the title heir of Quanjiao County.

sentences.zh: 預誅隱太子尤力。

translations.literal: He took exceptional part in executing the Hidden Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He played an outstanding part in the execution of the Hidden Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 王即位，拜左衛將軍，進封潞國公，邑千戶。

translations.literal: When the Prince acceded, Junji was appointed Left Guard General, advanced to Duke of Lu with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became emperor, he was appointed Left Guard General and advanced to Duke of Lu with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，遷兵部尚書，俄檢校吏部尚書，參議朝政。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan he was transferred to Minister of War; soon he was made acting Minister of Personnel and took part in deliberating court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenguan (630) he was made Minister of War, and shortly thereafter acting Minister of Personnel, joining in deliberations on state policy.

sentences.zh: 李靖討吐谷渾，以君集為積石道行軍總管。

translations.literal: When Li Jing campaigned against Tuyuhun, Junji was made campaign commander of the Jishi Route.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing marched against Tuyuhun, Junji was appointed campaign commander on the Jishi route.

sentences.zh: 師次鄯州，議所向。

translations.literal: The army halted at Shan Prefecture and debated which direction to take.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Shan Prefecture while commanders debated their line of advance.

sentences.zh: 君集曰：「王師已至，而賊不走險，天贊我也。

translations.literal: Junji said: "The royal army has arrived, yet the enemy does not flee into difficult terrain — Heaven is aiding us.
translations.idiomatic: Junji said, "Our army is already here, yet the enemy has not withdrawn into difficult country — Heaven itself is aiding us.

sentences.zh: 若以精兵掩不備，彼不我虞，必有大利。

translations.literal: If we use elite troops to strike them unprepared, they will not expect us and there will surely be great gain.
translations.idiomatic: If we send picked troops against them while they are unprepared, they will not be on their guard, and the advantage will be great.

sentences.zh: 若遁岨山谷，克之實難。

translations.literal: If they escape into rugged mountains and valleys, subduing them will truly be difficult."
translations.idiomatic: If they slip away into steep mountains and ravines, defeating them will be far harder."

sentences.zh: 」靖然其計，簡銳士，約齎深入，追及其眾於庫山，大戰，破之，進會大非川，平其國。

translations.literal: " Jing approved his plan, selected crack troops, agreed on light baggage for a deep advance, overtook the enemy host at Mount Ku, fought a great battle and routed them, advanced to join at the Great Non River, and pacified their state.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Jing approved the plan, picked elite troops, arranged for a light supply train on a deep thrust, caught the enemy at Mount Ku in a major battle and broke them, then pressed on to the Great Non River and brought their state to submission.

sentences.zh: 會詔世封功臣，授陳州刺史，更封陳；

translations.literal: It happened that an edict enfeoffed meritorious ministers for generations; he was given Chen Prefecture and his fief was changed to Chen;
translations.idiomatic: An edict then granted hereditary fiefs to meritorious ministers; he was appointed prefect of Chen and his title was changed to Duke of Chen;

sentences.zh: 群臣不願封，進吏部尚書。

translations.literal: the assembled ministers did not wish to accept fiefs, and he was advanced to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: but when the ministers as a body declined enfeoffment, he was promoted to Minister of Personnel instead.

sentences.zh: 君集本以行伍奮，不知學；

translations.literal: Junji had originally risen from the ranks and knew nothing of learning;
translations.idiomatic: Junji had risen from the ranks and had no schooling;

sentences.zh: 後貴，益自喜，好書。

translations.literal: after he became eminent he grew all the more pleased with himself and took to books.
translations.idiomatic: once he had grown eminent he became still more self-satisfied and took up reading.

sentences.zh: 及典選，分明課最，有譽于時。

translations.literal: When he took charge of selection, he distinguished grades clearly and won reputation in his day.
translations.idiomatic: When he oversaw official selection he ranked candidates clearly by merit and won a strong reputation at court.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃圍松州，授當彌道行軍大總管以擊之。

translations.literal: When Tibet besieged Song Prefecture, he was made campaign commander of the Dangmi Route to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans besieged Song Prefecture, he was appointed campaign commander on the Dangmi route to drive them off.

sentences.zh: 高昌不臣，拜交河道行軍大總管出討。

translations.literal: Gaochang was disloyal; he was appointed campaign commander of the Jiaohe Route and sent out to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaochang rebelled, he was made campaign commander on the Jiaohe route and sent to subdue the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 王曲文泰笑曰：「唐去我七千里，磧鹵二千里無水草，冬風裂肌，夏風如焚，行賈至者百之一，安能致大兵乎？

translations.literal: King Qu Wentai of Gaochang laughed and said: "Tang is seven thousand li from us; for two thousand li of desert and salt wastes there is no grass or water; winter winds tear the flesh, summer winds burn like fire; of merchants who come, only one in a hundred arrives — how can they bring a great army?
translations.idiomatic: King Qu Wentai of Gaochang laughed and said, "Tang lies seven thousand li away; two thousand li of desert and salt flats have neither grass nor water; winter winds flay the skin and summer winds scorch like flame; only one merchant in a hundred who sets out ever arrives — how could they field a great army?

sentences.zh: 使能頓吾城下一再旬，食盡當潰，吾且系而虜之。

translations.literal: Even if they could camp beneath our walls for a fortnight or so, when provisions were exhausted they would surely collapse, and I shall bind and capture them."
translations.idiomatic: Even if they could sit under our walls for a fortnight, once their food ran out they would break; then I would take them bound as captives."

sentences.zh: 」君集次磧口，而文泰死，子智盛襲位。

translations.literal: " Junji halted at the desert pass; Wentai died and his son Zhicheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: " Junji encamped at the desert pass; Wentai died, and his son Zhicheng took the throne.

sentences.zh: 進營柳穀，候騎言國方葬死君，諸將請襲之。

translations.literal: Advancing he encamped at Willow Valley; scouts reported the state was burying the dead king, and the generals asked to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and encamped at Willow Valley; scouts reported that the kingdom was burying its late ruler, and the generals urged a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 君集曰：「不可，天子以高昌驕慢，使吾龔行天罰，今襲人於墟墓間，非問罪也。

translations.literal: Junji said: "It cannot be done. The Son of Heaven, because Gaochang was arrogant and disrespectful, sent us to carry out Heaven's punishment; to strike people amid ruins and tombs is not an army of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Junji said, "No. The Son of Heaven sent us because Gaochang was arrogant and insolent, to execute Heaven's punishment; to attack people amid funeral mounds is not how one brings a criminal state to account.

sentences.zh: 」於是鼓而前。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he beat the drums and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: " He had the drums sounded and marched forward.

sentences.zh: 賊嬰城自守，遣諭之，不下。

translations.literal: The rebels clung to the city in defense; he sent envoys to persuade them, but they would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy shut themselves in the city; he sent messengers to summon their surrender, but they refused.

sentences.zh: 乃刊木塞塹，引撞車毀其堞，飛石如雨，所向無敢當，因拔其城，俘男女七千，進圍都城，初，文泰與西突厥欲穀設約，有急相援。

translations.literal: He then felled trees to fill the moat, drew up battering rams to destroy the parapets, and flying stones fell like rain — none dared stand before him; thus he stormed the city and captured seven thousand men and women, then advanced to besiege the capital. Earlier, Wentai had agreed with Yipishe of the Western Turks that in emergency they would aid each other.
translations.idiomatic: He felled timber to fill the moat, brought up battering rams to smash the battlements, and stones flew like rain so that nothing could withstand him; he took the city and seized seven thousand men and women, then pressed on to besiege the capital. Earlier, Wentai had made a pact with Yipishe of the Western Turks to support each other in crisis.

sentences.zh: 及是，欲穀設益懼，西走，智盛失援，乃降。

translations.literal: At this Yipishe grew all the more fearful, fled west, Zhicheng lost support, and thereupon submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yipishe grew still more afraid, fled westward, Zhicheng lost his ally, and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 高昌平，君集刻石紀功還。

translations.literal: Gaochang was pacified; Junji carved stone to record his merit and returned.
translations.idiomatic: With Gaochang pacified, Junji set up a stone monument to record his achievements and returned.

sentences.zh: 初，君集配沒罪人不以聞，又私取珍寶、婦女，將士因亦盜入，不能制。

translations.literal: Earlier, Junji had assigned convicts without reporting it, and privately took treasures and women; the officers and soldiers therefore also plundered, and he could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had distributed condemned men without reporting it to the throne, and privately seized treasures and women; his troops followed suit with looting he could not control.

sentences.zh: 及還京師，有司劾之，詔君集詣獄簿對。

translations.literal: When he returned to the capital, the responsible offices impeached him; an edict ordered Junji to the prison to answer the ledger.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to the capital the responsible offices impeached him, and an edict ordered Junji to prison to answer the charges.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎岑文本諫曰：「高昌之罪，議者以其遐遠，欲置度外，唯陛下奮獨見之明，授決勝之略，君集得指期平殄。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Cen Wuben remonstrated, saying: "Gaochang's offense — deliberators, because it was remote, wished to set it beyond concern; only Your Majesty exerted unique insight and entrusted the strategy for certain victory, and Junji was able to destroy them within the appointed term.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat Cen Wuben remonstrated: "On Gaochang's crime, court opinion, because the kingdom was remote, would have let the matter pass; only Your Majesty, with singular resolve, entrusted the strategy for decisive victory, and Junji brought them to ruin within the appointed time.

sentences.zh: 今推勞將帥，從征之人悉蒙重賞，未逾數日，更以屬吏，天下聞之，謂陛下錄過遺功，無以勸後。

translations.literal: Now you shift the merit to the commanders, and all who followed the campaign received heavy rewards; within a few days you again treat him as a subordinate official — when the realm hears of it, they will say Your Majesty records faults and forgets achievements, and there is no means to encourage those who come after.
translations.idiomatic: Now you have lavished rewards on the commanders and every man who marched; within days you hand him over to the clerks — the realm will say Your Majesty remembers faults and forgets merit, and nothing will encourage those who follow.

sentences.zh: 且古之出師，克敵有重賞，不勝蒙顯戮。

translations.literal: Moreover, in antiquity when armies went forth, defeating the enemy brought heavy reward; failing to win brought conspicuous execution.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in antiquity armies that conquered received great rewards, and armies that failed suffered open execution.

sentences.zh: 當其有功也，雖貪財縱欲，尚蒙爵邑；

translations.literal: When they had achievement, though they were greedy for wealth and indulged desire, they still received fiefs and estates;
translations.idiomatic: When they succeeded, even if they were greedy and licentious, they still received titles and estates;

sentences.zh: 其無功也，雖勤躬潔己，不免鈇鉞。

translations.literal: when they had no achievement, though they were diligent in person and pure in conduct, they did not escape axe and halberd.
translations.idiomatic: when they failed, even if they were scrupulous and self-denying, they did not escape the axe.

sentences.zh: 故曰：'記人之功，忘人之過，宜為君者也。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: 'Record a man's achievements, forget his faults — this is fitting for a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "Record a man's achievements and forget his faults — that is what befits a ruler.

sentences.zh: '昔李廣利貪不愛卒，陳湯盜所收康居財物，二主皆赦其罪，封侯賜金。

translations.literal: ' Formerly Li Guangli was greedy and did not care for his soldiers; Chen Tang stole goods taken from Kangju — both rulers pardoned their crimes, enfeoffed them as marquises, and bestowed gold.
translations.idiomatic: " In the past Li Guangli was greedy and indifferent to his troops; Chen Tang stole booty taken from Kangju — both emperors pardoned them, made them marquises, and gave them gold.

sentences.zh: 夫將帥之臣，廉慎少而貪沒多。

translations.literal: Among generals and commanders, the incorrupt and cautious are few while the greedy and grasping are many.
translations.idiomatic: Among commanders, the scrupulous are few and the grasping are many.

sentences.zh: 軍法曰：'使智，使勇，使貪，使愚。

translations.literal: Military law says: 'Use the wise, use the brave, use the greedy, use the foolish.
translations.idiomatic: Military law says: "Employ the wise, employ the brave, employ the greedy, employ the foolish.

sentences.zh: 故智者樂立其功，勇者好行其志，貪者邀趨其利，愚者不計其死。

translations.literal: Thus the wise delight in establishing their merit, the brave love to carry out their will, the greedy hurry after profit, and the foolish do not reckon with death.
translations.idiomatic: The wise delight in winning merit, the brave in fulfilling their purpose, the greedy in rushing after gain, and the foolish in giving no thought to death.

sentences.zh: '是以前聖使人，必收所長而棄所短。

translations.literal: ' Therefore the former sages in employing men always took their strengths and discarded their weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: " That is why the sage rulers of old, in employing men, always took their strengths and set aside their faults.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜申宥君集，俾復朝列，以勸有功。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should extend pardon to Junji, restore him to the court ranks, and thereby encourage those with achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should extend clemency to Junji, restore him to court office, and thereby encourage merit hereafter.

sentences.zh: 」帝寤，釋不問。

translations.literal: " The Emperor came to his senses and released him without further inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took the point and released him without further proceedings.

sentences.zh: 君集自恃有功，以它罪被系，居怏怏不平。

translations.literal: Junji, relying on his achievements, had been bound on another charge and lived resentful and ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Junji, confident in his achievements, had nevertheless been detained on other charges and brooded in discontent.

sentences.zh: 會張亮出洛州都督，君集謬激說曰：「何為見排？

translations.literal: It happened that Zhang Liang was leaving his post as military governor of Luo Prefecture; Junji falsely provoked him, saying: "Why are you being pushed aside?
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Liang was departing as military governor of Luo, Junji goaded him falsely: "Why are you being pushed aside?

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「公排我，尚誰咎？

translations.literal: " Liang said: "You pushed me aside — whom else should I blame?
translations.idiomatic: " Liang said, "You pushed me aside — whom else should I blame?

sentences.zh: 」君集曰：「我平一國還，觸天子嗔，何能排君？

translations.literal: " Junji said: "I pacified a state and returned, yet provoked the Son of Heaven's anger — how could I push you aside?
translations.idiomatic: " Junji said, "I subdued a kingdom and returned only to provoke the emperor's anger — how could I have pushed you aside?

sentences.zh: 」因攘袂曰：「鬱鬱不可活，能反乎？

translations.literal: " Then he rolled up his sleeves and said: "This suffocating life is unbearable — can we rebel?
translations.idiomatic: " He rolled up his sleeves and said, "Life like this is unbearable — shall we rebel?

sentences.zh: 當與公反。

translations.literal: I shall rebel with you."
translations.idiomatic: I will rebel with you."

sentences.zh: 」亮密以聞。

translations.literal: " Liang secretly reported it.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang reported it to the throne in secret.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿與君集皆功臣，今獨相語而無左驗，奈何？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You and Junji are both meritorious ministers; now you speak to each other alone with no corroborating proof — what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You and Junji are both meritorious ministers; now you tell me of words spoken between you alone, with no corroboration — what am I to do?

sentences.zh: 」秘不發，待君集如初。

translations.literal: " He kept it secret and did not act, treating Junji as before.
translations.idiomatic: " He kept the matter secret and continued to treat Junji as before.

sentences.zh: 皇太子承乾數有過，慮廢，知君集犯望，因其婿賀蘭楚石為千牛，私引君集入，問自安計。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Chengan had repeatedly offended and feared deposition; knowing Junji was disaffected, through his son-in-law Helan Chushi, who served as Palace Attendant, he privately brought Junji in and asked for a plan to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Chengan had repeatedly given offense and feared deposition; knowing Junji was discontent, he used his son-in-law Helan Chushi, a Palace Attendant, to bring Junji in secretly and ask how he might secure his position.

sentences.zh: 君集舉手謂曰：「此手當為殿下用之。

translations.literal: Junji raised his hand and said: "This hand ought to be used for Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: Junji raised his hand and said, "This hand is meant to serve Your Highness.

sentences.zh: 」又遣楚石語承乾曰：「魏王得愛，陛下若有詔召，願毋輕入。

translations.literal: " He also sent Chushi to tell Chengan: "The Prince of Wei enjoys favor; if Your Majesty should issue a summons, I beg you not to enter lightly.
translations.idiomatic: " He also sent Chushi to warn Chengan: "The Prince of Wei is in favor; if the emperor should summon you, do not go lightly.

sentences.zh: 」承乾納之。

translations.literal: " Chengan accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: " Chengan took the advice.

sentences.zh: 然君集常畏謀泄，忽忽不自安，或中夕驚吒，妻怪之，曰：「公，國大臣，何為爾？

translations.literal: Yet Junji constantly feared the plot would leak; he was restless and ill at ease, and sometimes cried out in alarm at midnight. His wife wondered at it and said: "Sir, you are a great minister of state — why act like this?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Junji lived in constant fear that the plot would leak; he was restless and uneasy, and sometimes cried out in the night. His wife was alarmed and said, "You are a great minister of state — why behave like this?

sentences.zh: 若有所負，宜自歸，首領尚可全。

translations.literal: If you bear some burden on your conscience, you ought to surrender yourself; your head may still be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: If you have something on your conscience, you should confess; your life may still be spared."

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: " He would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " He would not listen.

sentences.zh: 承乾事覺，捕君集下獄。

translations.literal: When Chengan's affair was exposed, Junji was seized and cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengan's plot was exposed, Junji was arrested and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 楚石告狀，帝自臨問，曰：「我不欲令刀筆吏辱公。

translations.literal: Chushi lodged the accusation; the Emperor came in person to question him, saying: "I do not wish clerks with their pens to humiliate you.
translations.idiomatic: Chushi laid information against him; the emperor questioned him in person, saying, "I do not wish petty clerks to humiliate you.

sentences.zh: 君集辭窮不能對。

translations.literal: Junji's words were exhausted and he could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Junji had no answer left to give.

sentences.zh: 帝語群臣曰：「君集于國有功，朕不忍置諸法，將丐其命，公卿其許我乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor said to the assembled ministers: "Junji has merit for the state; I cannot bear to subject him to the law and wish to beg his life — will you, lords and ministers, grant me this?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the assembled ministers, "Junji has served the state with merit; I cannot bear to hand him to the law and wish to beg his life — will you grant it?

sentences.zh: 」君臣皆曰：「君集罪大逆不道，請論如法。

translations.literal: " Ruler and ministers all said: "Junji's crime is great rebellion and impiety; we ask that he be judged according to law.
translations.idiomatic: " They replied as one, "Junji's crime is treason of the gravest kind; let him be judged by law.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃謂曰：「與公訣矣，今而後，徒見公遺像已！

translations.literal: " The Emperor then said to him: "I take leave of you; hereafter I shall see only your portrait!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then said to him, "We part here; hereafter I shall see only your portrait!

sentences.zh: 」因泣下，遂斬之，籍其家。

translations.literal: " Weeping, he then had him executed and registered his household for confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: " He wept, then had him executed and confiscated his household.

sentences.zh: 君集臨刑色不變，謂監吏曰：「我豈反者乎？

translations.literal: Facing execution Junji's countenance did not change; he said to the supervising officer: "Am I truly a rebel?
translations.idiomatic: At the block Junji's face did not change; he told the officer, "Am I truly a rebel?

sentences.zh: 蹉跌至此。

translations.literal: I have stumbled to this point.
translations.idiomatic: I have stumbled to this pass.

sentences.zh: 然嘗為將，破二國，若言之陛下，丐一子以守祭祀。

translations.literal: Yet I once was a general and broke two states; if you speak to His Majesty, beg one son to maintain the sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I was once a general who subdued two kingdoms; if you speak to His Majesty, beg one son to keep the ancestral rites."

sentences.zh: 」帝聞，原其妻及一子，徙嶺表。

translations.literal: " When the Emperor heard, he pardoned his wife and one son and banished them beyond the Ling ranges.
translations.idiomatic: " On hearing this, the emperor spared his wife and one son and exiled them to the far south.

sentences.zh: 始，帝命李靖教君集兵法，既而奏：「靖且反，兵之隱微，不以示臣。

translations.literal: Earlier the Emperor had ordered Li Jing to teach Junji military arts; afterward Junji memorialized: "Jing is about to rebel — the subtle points of warfare he does not show me.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had Li Jing instruct Junji in the art of war; afterward Junji reported, "Jing is on the verge of rebellion — he withholds the subtle points of strategy from me.

sentences.zh: 」帝以讓靖，靖曰：「方中原無事，臣之所教，足以制四夷，而求盡臣術，此君集欲反耳。

translations.literal: " The Emperor reproached Jing; Jing said: "While the central plains were untroubled, what I taught was enough to control the four barbarians; to seek all my art — this shows Junji intends rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor reproached Jing; Jing said, "While the heartland was at peace, what I taught was enough to subdue the four quarters; to demand every secret of my craft — that shows Junji meant to rebel.

sentences.zh: 靖為右僕射，君集為兵部尚書，同還省，君集馬過門數步乃覺，靖語人曰：「君集其有異慮乎？

translations.literal: Jing was Right Vice Director and Junji Minister of War; returning together to their offices, Junji's horse passed the gate several paces before he noticed — Jing said to others: "Does Junji harbor other designs?
translations.idiomatic: Jing was Right Vice Director and Junji Minister of War; riding back together from court, Junji's horse passed the gate several paces before he reined in — Jing remarked, "Does Junji have something else on his mind?

sentences.zh: 」後果如言。

translations.literal: " Later events proved his words.
translations.idiomatic: " Events later bore him out.

sentences.zh: 張亮張亮，鄭州滎陽人。

translations.literal: __FORCETOC__Zhang Liang — Zhang Liang, a native of Xingyang in Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: __FORCETOC__Zhang Liang was a native of Xingyang in Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 起畎畝，志趣奇譎，雖外敦厚而內不情。

translations.literal: He rose from the fields; his aims were strange and devious — though outwardly generous and solid, inwardly he was without feeling.
translations.idiomatic: He came up from the plowlands with eccentric ambitions; though he seemed outwardly mild and honest, inwardly he was cold and calculating.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，李密略地滎、汴，亮從之，未甚甄識。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye in Sui, Li Mi seized lands in Xing and Bian; Liang followed him but was not greatly distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, when Li Mi seized the Xing and Bian region, Liang joined him but won little notice.

sentences.zh: 時軍中有謀叛去者，亮輒以告，密愛其誠，乃署驃騎將軍，隸李勣。

translations.literal: When in the army some plotted to desert, Liang always reported it; Mi loved his loyalty and appointed him Rapid Cavalry General under Li Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever men in the army plotted to desert, Liang reported them; Mi valued his loyalty and made him Rapid Cavalry General under Li Ji.

sentences.zh: 勣以黎陽歸，亮頗佐佑之，擢鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: When Ji surrendered Liyang, Liang greatly assisted him and was promoted to prefect of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji surrendered Liyang, Liang gave him strong support and was promoted to prefect of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 會王世充取鄭，亮提孤軍不敢入，亡命共城山。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong seized Zheng, Liang led an isolated army and dared not enter; he fled to Mount Gongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong took Zheng, Liang held an isolated force and dared not enter the city; he fled to Mount Gongcheng.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校定州別駕。

translations.literal: Soon he was made acting vice prefect of Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed acting vice prefect of Ding.

sentences.zh: 勣討劉黑闥，使亮守相州，賊方盛，棄城遁。

translations.literal: When Ji campaigned against Liu Heita, he had Liang defend Xiang Prefecture; the rebels were at their height and Liang abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji campaigned against Liu Heita, he left Liang to hold Xiang Prefecture; the rebels were at their peak, and Liang abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡以亮沈果有謀，白秦王，引為車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling, because Liang was deep, resolute, and resourceful, informed the Prince of Qin and had him brought in as Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling, seeing Liang's depth, resolve, and cunning, recommended him to the Prince of Qin, who made him Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 隱太子將作難，命亮統左右千人之洛陽，陰結山東豪傑以備變。

translations.literal: The Hidden Crown Prince was about to raise trouble; he ordered Liang to command a thousand men of the Left and Right Guards at Luoyang and secretly rally Shandong magnates against contingencies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hidden Crown Prince plotted rebellion, he ordered Liang to command a thousand guardsmen at Luoyang and secretly rally powerful men of the east against any turn of events.

sentences.zh: 齊王告亮反，高祖以屬吏詰訊，終無所言，乃得釋。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi reported Liang's rebellion; Gaozu handed him to officials for interrogation, but he finally said nothing and was released.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi accused Liang of rebellion; Gaozu had him interrogated by the responsible offices, but Liang said nothing throughout and was released.

sentences.zh: 王即位，除右衛將軍，封長平郡公。

translations.literal: When the Prince acceded, Liang was made Right Guard General and enfeoffed as Duke of Changping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became emperor, he was made Right Guard General and enfeoffed as Duke of Changping.

sentences.zh: 累遷御史大夫，進封鄅國公，食益州戶五百。

translations.literal: He was promoted through Censor-in-Chief and advanced to Duke of Yu state with an income of five hundred households in Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Censor-in-Chief, was advanced to Duke of Yu, and drew income from five hundred households in Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歷豳夏汭鄜三州都督、相州長史，徙鄖國。

translations.literal: He served as military governor of Bin, Xia, Rui, and Fu prefectures and as chief administrator of Xiang, then was transferred to Duke of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He served as military governor of Bin, Xia, Rui, and Fu and as chief administrator of Xiang, then was transferred to the title Duke of Yun.

sentences.zh: 召拜工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 亮為政多伺察，發擿隱微，示神明，抑強恤弱，所至有績。

translations.literal: In governing Liang much surveilled and exposed hidden matters, displaying sagacity, restraining the strong and succoring the weak — wherever he went he had achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In office he relied heavily on surveillance, ferreting out hidden wrongdoing and projecting an air of omniscience, curbing the powerful and aiding the weak; wherever he served he left a record of success.

sentences.zh: 拜太子詹事，出為洛州都督。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then sent out as military governor of Luo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then sent out as military governor of Luo.

sentences.zh: 侯君集已誅，以刑部尚書參預朝政。

translations.literal: After Hou Junji was executed, he was made Minister of Justice and took part in court deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Junji's execution he was made Minister of Justice and joined in deliberations on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 時茂州俚童張仲文自稱天子，有司論斥乘輿有罪當死，攝刑部尚書韋挺奏：「童乃妖言，無死坐。

translations.literal: At the time a Li boy of Mao Prefecture, Zhang Zhongwen, styled himself Son of Heaven; the responsible offices judged that denouncing the imperial carriage was a capital crime; Acting Minister of Justice Wei Ting memorialized: "The boy spoke demonic words — there is no capital offense.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a Li youth of Mao Prefecture, Zhang Zhongwen, proclaimed himself emperor; the responsible offices held that insulting the imperial carriage warranted death; Acting Minister of Justice Wei Ting argued, "A child's wild talk does not carry the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒曰：「爾作威福於下，而歸虐朕耶！

translations.literal: " The Emperor angrily said: "You wield authority below and then lay cruelty on me!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor flared up: "You play the tyrant below and then make me out the cruel one!

sentences.zh: 」挺失據趨出。

translations.literal: " Ting lost his composure and hurried out.
translations.idiomatic: " Ting lost his composure and fled the hall.

sentences.zh: 亮為挺直之，帝曰：「公欲取剛正名乎？

translations.literal: Liang spoke up for Ting; the Emperor said: "Do you wish to win a reputation for stern integrity?
translations.idiomatic: Liang spoke up for Ting; the emperor said, "Are you trying to win a name for righteous remonstrance?

sentences.zh: 」亮不謝，帝寤曰：「甯屈我，以申公之請。

translations.literal: " Liang did not apologize; the Emperor came to his senses and said: "I would rather bend myself to grant your request.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang did not back down; the emperor recovered and said, "I would rather yield than refuse your plea.

sentences.zh: 」童免死。

translations.literal: " The boy was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: " The boy was spared.

sentences.zh: 帝將伐高麗，亮頻諫，不納，因自請行，詔為平壤道行軍大總管。

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to campaign against Goguryeo; Liang remonstrated repeatedly but was not heeded; he therefore volunteered to go and was ordered campaign commander of the Pingrang Route.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor prepared to campaign against Goguryeo, Liang remonstrated repeatedly in vain, then volunteered for the field and was appointed campaign commander on the Pingrang route.

sentences.zh: 引兵自東萊浮海，襲破沙卑城，進至建安，營壁未立，賊奄至，亮不知所為，踞胡床直視無所言，眾謂其勇，得自安。

translations.literal: He led troops from Donglai by sea, stormed and took Shabie city, advanced to Jian'an; the camp walls were not yet set when rebels suddenly arrived. Liang did not know what to do — he sat on a barbarian folding chair, staring straight ahead and saying nothing; the troops took this for courage and regained composure.
translations.idiomatic: He led his army from Donglai by sea, stormed Shabie, and advanced to Jian'an; before the camp was fortified the enemy fell upon them. Liang sat motionless on a folding camp chair, staring ahead without a word; the men mistook this for composure and steadied themselves.

sentences.zh: 於是副將張金樹鼓於軍，士奮擊，因破賊。

translations.literal: Thereupon his deputy Zhang Jinshu beat the drums in the army; the soldiers fought fiercely and thus routed the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: His deputy Zhang Jinshu then beat the drums; the troops charged with spirit and broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 及從帝還，至并州，乃得罪。

translations.literal: When he followed the Emperor back and reached Bing Prefecture, he then fell into disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march, when the army reached Bingzhou, he fell into disgrace.

sentences.zh: 初，亮棄故妻，更娶李氏。

translations.literal: Earlier Liang had abandoned his former wife and married again, taking the Lady Li.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had cast off his first wife and married a Lady Li.

sentences.zh: 李妒悍，私通歌兒，養為子，名慎幾。

translations.literal: Li was jealous and fierce; she secretly kept a song-boy, raised him as a son, and named him Shenji.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li was jealous and overbearing; she secretly kept a singing boy, adopted him as a son, and named him Shenji.

sentences.zh: 亮子顗數諫止，亮不納。

translations.literal: Liang's son Yan repeatedly remonstrated but Liang would not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's son Yan remonstrated again and again, but Liang would not listen.

sentences.zh: 李好左道，交通巫覡，橈政事。

translations.literal: Li loved heterodox ways, trafficked with shamans and sorcerers, and bent government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li dabbled in heterodox cults, consorted with shamans, and meddled in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 亮為相州，假子公孫節以讖有「弓長之主當別都」，亮自以相舊都，「弓長」其姓，陰有怪謀。

translations.literal: When Liang was at Xiang Prefecture, his foster son Gongsun Jie cited a prophecy saying "the lord of Gong-Zhang shall have a separate capital"; Liang took Xiang as an ancient capital, "Gong-Zhang" as his surname Zhang, and secretly harbored strange designs.
translations.idiomatic: While Liang governed Xiang, his foster son Gongsun Jie cited a prophecy that "the lord of bow-and-long shall rule a separate capital"; Liang noted that Xiang was an ancient capital and that "bow-long" (gong-zhang) echoed his surname Zhang, and secretly nursed treasonous ambitions.

sentences.zh: 術家程公穎者，亮素與厚，陰謂曰：「君前言陛下真天下主，何其神邪！

translations.literal: A practitioner Cheng Gongying, with whom Liang had long been close, Liang said to in secret: "You once said His Majesty was the true Son of Heaven under Heaven — how divine!
translations.idiomatic: A diviner named Cheng Gongying, whom Liang had long favored, heard him say in private, "You once declared that His Majesty was the true ruler of all under Heaven — how prescient you were!

sentences.zh: 」公穎內曉，即稱亮臥若龍，當大貴。

translations.literal: " Gongying understood inwardly and at once said Liang in repose was like a dragon and would attain great eminence.
translations.idiomatic: " Gongying understood at once and declared that Liang in repose was like a dragon and destined for greatness.

sentences.zh: 亮曰：「國家殆必亂，吾臂龍鱗奮矣，慎幾且大貴。

translations.literal: Liang said: "The state will surely fall into disorder; the dragon scales on my arm are stirring — Shenji too will attain great eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Liang said, "The realm will surely fall into chaos; the dragon scales on my arm are stirring, and Shenji too will rise high.

sentences.zh: 」公孫常者，節兄也，亮謂曰：「吾有妾，相者云必為諸王姬。

translations.literal: " Gongsun Chang was Jie's elder brother; Liang said to him: "I have a concubine whom diviners say will surely become a prince's consort.
translations.idiomatic: " Gongsun Chang was Jie's elder brother; Liang told him, "I have a concubine whom fortune-tellers say is destined to marry a prince.

sentences.zh: 」常曰：「我兄子大品言，有神告公名在讖書。

translations.literal: " Chang said: "My brother's son Dapin says a spirit told him your name is in the prophecy books.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang said, "My nephew Dapin says a spirit revealed that your name appears in the prophecy texts.

sentences.zh: 」亮悅。

translations.literal: " Liang was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang was delighted.

sentences.zh: 會陝人常德發其謀，並言亮養假子五百。

translations.literal: It happened that Chang De of Shan exposed his plot and also said Liang had raised five hundred foster sons.
translations.idiomatic: Then a man of Shan named Chang De exposed the plot and reported that Liang had raised five hundred foster sons.

sentences.zh: 帝使馬周案之，亮讕辭曰：「囚等畏死，見誣耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor had Ma Zhou investigate; Liang equivocated, saying: "These prisoners fear death and falsely accuse me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Ma Zhou investigate; Liang prevaricated: "These men fear death and have slandered me.

sentences.zh: 」因自陳佐命舊臣。

translations.literal: " He then declared himself an old minister who had aided the founding mandate.
translations.idiomatic: " He pleaded that he was an old minister who had helped establish the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「亮養子五百將何為？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "What were Liang's five hundred foster sons for?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What did you want with five hundred foster sons?

sentences.zh: 正欲反耳。

translations.literal: Precisely to rebel."
translations.idiomatic: To rebel, of course."

sentences.zh: 」詔百官議，皆言亮當誅。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered the officials to deliberate; all said Liang should be executed.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the officials to deliberate; all agreed Liang must die.

sentences.zh: 帝遣長孫無忌、房玄齡就獄謂曰：「法者，天下平，與公共為之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Zhangsun Wuji and Fang Xuanling to the prison to say: "Law is the balance of the realm; we fashioned it together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Zhangsun Wuji and Fang Xuanling to the prison with the message: "Law is the foundation of peace in the realm, and we made it together.

sentences.zh: 公不自修，乃至此，將奈何？

translations.literal: You did not restrain yourself and have come to this — what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: You would not restrain yourself, and matters have come to this — what can be done?

sentences.zh: 」於是斬西市，籍其家。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was executed at the western market and his household was registered for confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: " He was executed at the western market and his property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 薛萬鈞薛萬均，本燉煌人，後徙京兆咸陽。

translations.literal: __FORCETOC__Xue Wanjun — Xue Wanjun, originally a man of Dunhuang, later moved to Xianyang in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: __FORCETOC__Xue Wanjun was originally from Dunhuang and later moved to Xianyang in the capital district.

sentences.zh: 父世雄，大業末為涿郡太守，萬均與弟萬徹因客幽州，以材武為羅藝所厚善。

translations.literal: His father Shixiong, at the end of Daye was prefect of Zhuo commandery; Wanjun and his younger brother Wanche lodged in You Prefecture and, for martial talent, were greatly favored by Luo Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shixiong served as prefect of Zhuo at the end of the Sui; Wanjun and his younger brother Wanche sojourned in Youzhou, where their martial prowess won the deep favor of Luo Yi.

sentences.zh: 與藝歸款，高祖授萬均上柱國、永安郡公。

translations.literal: When he and Yi submitted, Gaozu granted Wanjun Supreme Pillar of State and Duke of Yong'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi submitted to Tang, Gaozu made Wanjun Supreme Pillar of State and Duke of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 竇建德帥眾十萬寇范陽，藝迎拒之。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande led a hundred thousand men to raid Fanyang; Yi went out to meet and resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande led a hundred thousand men against Fanyang; Yi marched out to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 萬均曰：「眾寡不敵，宜以計勝。

translations.literal: Wanjun said: "We are unequal in numbers and cannot match them head-on; we should win by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Wanjun said, "We are too few to meet them directly; we must win by strategy.

sentences.zh: 」即教藝羸兵阻水以誘之，萬均自以精騎百匿城左。

translations.literal: " He then taught Yi to use weak troops to block the water and lure them; Wanjun himself took a hundred elite horsemen and hid to the left of the city.
translations.idiomatic: " He had Yi post weak troops at the river to lure the enemy while he himself hid a hundred picked horsemen to the city's left.

sentences.zh: 建德師度水，邀半度擊之，大敗其眾。

translations.literal: Jiande's army crossed the water; when they were halfway across he intercepted and struck, routing their host.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiande's army was half across the water, he struck and routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 明年，建德以二十萬騎來攻，兵已緣堞，萬均與萬徹率死士百人出地道，掩擊其背，眾驚潰去。

translations.literal: The next year Jiande came with two hundred thousand horsemen; the enemy had already climbed the battlements when Wanjun and Wanche led a hundred death-defying men out through a tunnel, struck their rear by surprise, and the host fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Jiande returned with two hundred thousand cavalry; the enemy had already reached the walls when Wanjun and Wanche led a hundred picked men through a tunnel, struck from behind, and sent the host fleeing in panic.

sentences.zh: 秦王平劉黑闥，引萬均為右二護軍，北門長上。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin pacified Liu Heita, he brought Wanjun in as Second Protector of the Right and senior commander at the northern gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin suppressed Liu Heita, he made Wanjun Second Protector of the Right and senior commander at the northern palace gate.

sentences.zh: 柴紹之討梁師都也，以萬均為副，萬徹亦從。

translations.literal: When Chai Shao campaigned against Liang Shidu, he made Wanjun his deputy and Wanche also followed.
translations.idiomatic: On Chai Shao's campaign against Liang Shidu, Wanjun served as his deputy and Wanche accompanied them.

sentences.zh: 距朔方數十里，突厥兵驟至，王師卻，萬均兄弟橫擊之，斬其驍將，虜陣歡，乘之，俘殺相藉。

translations.literal: Several tens of li from Shuofang, Turk forces suddenly arrived; the royal army fell back; the Wanjun brothers struck across their line, beheaded their fierce general, the barbarian formation wavered, they pressed the advantage, and captives and slain lay piled one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: A few dozen li from Shuofang, Turk forces suddenly appeared and the Tang army gave ground; the brothers charged across the enemy line, killed their boldest commander, threw the Turk formation into disorder, and pressed the attack until captives and corpses lay heaped together.

sentences.zh: 突厥走，遂圍師都。

translations.literal: The Turks fled, and they then besieged Shidu.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks fled, and they laid siege to Shidu.

sentences.zh: 諸將以城險未可下，萬均曰：「城中氣死，鼓不能聲，破亡兆也。

translations.literal: The generals held that the city's defenses made it impossible to take; Wanjun said: "Within the city the breath is dead — drums cannot sound; this is the omen of ruin.
translations.idiomatic: The generals thought the strong walls made the city untakable; Wanjun said, "The spirit inside is dead — their drums can scarcely sound; ruin is already upon them.

sentences.zh: 」既而賊果斬師都降。

translations.literal: " Before long the rebels indeed beheaded Shidu and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon the enemy killed Shidu and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 拜左屯衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Commander of the Unicorn Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commander of the Left Unicorn Guard.

sentences.zh: 俄為沃沮道行軍副總管，從李靖討吐谷渾。

translations.literal: Soon he was made deputy campaign commander of the Woju Route and followed Li Jing against Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became deputy commander on the Woju route and followed Li Jing against Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 軍次青海，萬均、萬徹各以百騎行前，卒與虜遇，萬均單騎馳突，無敢當者。

translations.literal: The army halted at Qinghai; Wanjun and Wanche each led a hundred horsemen ahead, suddenly met the barbarians, and Wanjun charged alone — none dared stand before him.
translations.idiomatic: At Qinghai, Wanjun and Wanche each led a hundred horsemen in advance; they suddenly met the enemy, and Wanjun charged alone with no one able to withstand him.

sentences.zh: 還語諸將曰：「賊易與。

translations.literal: Returning he told the generals: "The enemy are easy to deal with.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he told the generals, "These foes are easy to handle.

sentences.zh: 」復馳進擊，斬數千級，勇蓋三軍。

translations.literal: " He charged again, beheading several thousand; his valor surpassed the whole army.
translations.idiomatic: " He charged again, killing several thousand; his valor outshone the entire army.

sentences.zh: 追奔至積石山，大風折旗，萬均曰：「虜且來！

translations.literal: Pursuing the fugitives to Mount Jishi, a great wind snapped the banners; Wanjun said: "The barbarians are coming!
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing the fugitives to Mount Jishi, a fierce wind snapped the banners; Wanjun cried, "The enemy is upon us!

sentences.zh: 」乃勒兵。

translations.literal: " He then arrayed the troops.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately drew up the troops.

sentences.zh: 俄而虜至，萬均直前斬其將，眾遂潰，追至圖倫磧乃還，與靖會青海。

translations.literal: Before long the barbarians arrived; Wanjun went straight forward and beheaded their general; the host then collapsed; he pursued to the Tumen desert and returned, joining Jing at Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy soon appeared; Wanjun cut down their commander at the front, the host broke, and he pursued to the Tumen sands before returning to join Li Jing at Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 璽書勉勞，遷本衛大將軍。

translations.literal: An imperial letter commended and comforted him; he was transferred to Grand General of his guard.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial letter praised and rewarded him, and he was promoted to Grand General of his guard.

sentences.zh: 又副侯君集擊高昌，曲智盛堅守未下，萬均麾軍進，智盛懼，乃降。

translations.literal: He again served as deputy to Hou Junji against Gaochang; Qu Zhicheng held firm and would not yield; Wanjun commanded the army forward, Zhicheng feared, and thereupon submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He again served under Hou Junji against Gaochang; Qu Zhicheng held the city stubbornly until Wanjun pressed the attack, whereupon Zhicheng, in fear, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 進潞國公。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 會有訴萬均與高昌女子亂，太宗欲窮治。

translations.literal: It happened that someone accused Wanjun of misconduct with a Gaochang woman; Taizong wished to investigate thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Someone then accused him of improper relations with a Gaochang woman, and Taizong wished to pursue the matter to the end.

sentences.zh: 魏徵曰：君使臣以禮，若所訴實，罪且輕，虛則所失重矣。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said: "The ruler employs his ministers with propriety; if the accusation is true the crime is still light, but if false the loss would be grave.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said, "A ruler should treat his ministers with propriety; if the charge is true the offense is still slight, but if false the harm to the state would be great.

sentences.zh: 」詔勿治。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered that it not be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered that the matter not be pursued.

sentences.zh: 後帝幸芙蓉園，坐清宮不謹下獄，憂憤卒。

translations.literal: Later when the Emperor visited Furong Garden, he sat in the Pure Palace with impropriety and was cast into prison; distressed and resentful, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor visited Furong Garden, he was imprisoned for impropriety in the Pure Palace and died of grief and resentment.

sentences.zh: 帝驚悼，為舉哀，詔陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: The Emperor was startled and mourned, held mourning for him, and ordered burial at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was shocked and grieved, ordered mourning for him, and granted burial at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 後嘗賜群臣膜皮，及萬徹而誤呼萬均，愴然曰：「萬均朕勳舊，忽口其名，豈死者有知，冀此賜乎？

translations.literal: Later when bestowing membrane pelts on the ministers, reaching Wanche he mistakenly called Wanjun's name and said sorrowfully: "Wanjun was an old merit-holder of mine — suddenly to speak his name, do the dead have awareness and hope for this gift?
translations.idiomatic: Later, when distributing membrane pelts among the ministers, he came to Wanche but mistakenly called Wanjun's name and said in sorrow, "Wanjun was an old companion in merit — have I spoken his name because the dead still know, and hope for this gift?

sentences.zh: 」因命取焚之，舉坐感歎。

translations.literal: " He then ordered it taken and burned; all present were moved to sigh.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered it taken back and burned; the whole assembly was moved.

sentences.zh: 弟萬徹、萬淑、萬備。

translations.literal: Younger brothers Wanche, Wanshu, and Wanbei.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers were Wanche, Wanshu, and Wanbei.

sentences.zh: 弟 萬徹萬徹與萬均歸高祖，授車騎將軍、武安縣公，事隱太子。

translations.literal: Younger brother Wanche — Wanche and Wanjun submitted to Gaozu; he was appointed Cavalry General and Duke of Wu'an county, and served the Hidden Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Wanche — Wanche and Wanjun submitted to Gaozu; he was made Cavalry General and Duke of Wu'an and served the Hidden Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 太子誅，萬徹督宮兵戰武門，噪而趨秦府，眾失色；

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was executed, Wanche directed palace troops to fight at the Martial Gate, shouting as he rushed toward the Prince of Qin's residence; the crowd turned pale;
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was killed, Wanche led palace troops to fight at the Xuanwu Gate, shouting as he charged toward the Prince of Qin's residence; the onlookers turned pale;

sentences.zh: 乃示以太子首，然後去，與數十騎亡之南山。

translations.literal: they then showed him the crown prince's head; only then did he leave, and with several dozen horsemen fled to the southern hills.
translations.idiomatic: only when they showed him the crown prince's head did he withdraw, fleeing southward with a few dozen horsemen.

sentences.zh: 秦王數使貸諭，乃出謝。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin repeatedly sent envoys to reassure and instruct him; he then came out to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin sent envoys again and again to reassure him; at last he came out to submit.

sentences.zh: 王以其忠於所事，不之罪也。

translations.literal: The Prince, because he had been loyal to his charge, did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince spared him for loyalty to the charge he had served.

sentences.zh: 從李靖討突厥頡利可汗，以功授統軍，進爵郡公。

translations.literal: Following Li Jing against the Turk Jieli Khaghan, for merit he was made army commander and advanced to commandery duke.
translations.idiomatic: On Li Jing's campaign against the Turk khaghan Jieli, he was made army commander for his merit and advanced to commandery duke.

sentences.zh: 曆右衛將軍、蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: He served through Right Guard General and prefect of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Right Guard General and prefect of Pu.

sentences.zh: 副李勣擊薛延陀，與虜戰磧南，率數百騎為先鋒，繞擊陣後。

translations.literal: As deputy to Li Ji against Xue Yantuo, fighting the barbarians south of the desert, he led several hundred horsemen as vanguard and circled to strike behind their formation.
translations.idiomatic: As Li Ji's deputy against Xue Yantuo, fighting south of the desert, he led several hundred horsemen as vanguard and struck around to the enemy's rear.

sentences.zh: 虜顧見，遂潰，斬首三千級，獲馬萬五千，封一子為縣侯。

translations.literal: The barbarians looked back and saw him, then collapsed; three thousand heads were cut off and fifteen thousand horses taken; one son was enfeoffed as county marquis.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy saw him and broke; three thousand heads were taken and fifteen thousand horses captured; one son was enfeoffed as county marquis.

sentences.zh: 改左衛將軍，尚丹陽公主，加駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He was made Left Guard General, married Princess Danyang, and was added as Commandant Escort.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Left Guard General, married Princess Danyang, and was named Commandant Escort.

sentences.zh: 遷代州都督、右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military governor of Dai and Grand General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military governor of Dai and Grand General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗曰：「當今名將，唯李勣、江夏王道宗、萬徹而已。

translations.literal: Taizong once said: "Among famous generals of today, only Li Ji, the Prince of Jiangxia Daozong, and Wanche.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once said, "Among the famous generals of our day, only Li Ji, the Prince of Jiangxia Daozong, and Wanche count.

sentences.zh: 勣、道宗雖不能大勝，亦未嘗大敗；

translations.literal: Ji and Daozong, though they cannot win great victories, have never suffered great defeats;
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Daozong may not win resounding victories, but they have never suffered crushing defeats;

sentences.zh: 至萬徹，非大勝即大敗矣。

translations.literal: as for Wanche, if it is not a great victory it is a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Wanche, by contrast, wins big or loses big.

sentences.zh: 」貞觀二十二年，以青丘道行軍總管帥師三萬伐高麗，次鴨淥水，以奇兵襲大行城，與高麗步騎萬余戰，斬虜將所夫孫。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-second year of Zhenguan, as campaign commander of the Qingqiu Route he led thirty thousand troops against Goguryeo, halted at the Yalu, used picked troops in a surprise attack on Daxing city, fought more than ten thousand Goguryeo infantry and cavalry, and beheaded the barbarian general Suofusun.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twenty-second year of Zhenguan (648) he led thirty thousand men as campaign commander on the Qingqiu route against Goguryeo, halted at the Yalu, sent picked troops in a surprise raid on Daxing city, fought more than ten thousand Goguryeo foot and horse, and killed the enemy general Suofusun.

sentences.zh: 虜皆震恐，遂傅泊汋城。

translations.literal: The barbarians were all shaken with terror and thereupon moored at Bozhou city.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy was terrified and withdrew to Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 虜眾三萬來援，擊走之，拔其城。

translations.literal: Thirty thousand barbarians came to reinforce; he struck and drove them off and took the city.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty thousand reinforcements arrived; he defeated them and took the city.

sentences.zh: 萬徹在軍中，任氣不能下人，或有上書言狀者，帝愛其功，直加讓勖而已，即為焚書。

translations.literal: Wanche in the army was overbearing and would not defer to others; some memorialized on his conduct, but the Emperor loved his achievements and only rebuked and exhorted him, then burned the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In camp Wanche was domineering and would not defer to others; memorials were filed against him, but the emperor valued his achievements, rebuked him lightly, and burned the papers.

sentences.zh: 副將裴行方亦言其怨望。

translations.literal: His deputy Pei Xingfang also said he harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: His deputy Pei Xingfang also reported his discontent.

sentences.zh: 李勣曰：「萬徹位大將軍，親主婿，而內懷不平，罪當誅。

translations.literal: Li Ji said: "Wanche holds the rank of great general and is the emperor's son-in-law, yet inwardly he is discontent — the crime warrants execution.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji said, "Wanche is a great general and the emperor's son-in-law, yet he nurses resentment — the offense warrants death.

sentences.zh: 」因詔除籍徙邊，會赦，還。

translations.literal: " An edict removed him from the registers and banished him to the frontier; an amnesty followed and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict struck him from the rolls and banished him to the frontier; he returned under a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 高宗永徽二年，授甯州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui under Gaozong, he was appointed prefect of Ning.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yonghui (651) he was appointed prefect of Ning.

sentences.zh: 入朝，與房遺愛昵甚，因曰：「我雖病足，坐置京師，諸輩猶不敢動。

translations.literal: Entering court, he was very intimate with Fang Yiai and therefore said: "Though my feet are diseased, if I were seated in the capital the rest would not dare stir.
translations.idiomatic: On a court visit he grew very close to Fang Yiai and said, "Though my feet ail me, seated in the capital I could still keep the rest in check.

sentences.zh: 」遺愛曰：「若國有變，當與公共輔荊王。

translations.literal: " Yiai said: "If the state should change, I shall support the Prince of Jing with you.
translations.idiomatic: " Yiai said, "If the realm should change, I will join you in supporting the Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 」謀泄下獄，誅。

translations.literal: " The plot leaked; he was cast into prison and executed.
translations.idiomatic: " The plot was exposed; he was imprisoned and executed.

sentences.zh: 臨刑曰：「萬徹大健兒，留為國效死，安得坐遺愛殺之！

translations.literal: Facing execution he said: "Wanche is a great strong fellow — leave him to die for the state; how can he sit and be killed on Yiai's account!
translations.idiomatic: At the block he said, "Wanche is a stout warrior — let him die for the state; must he be killed because of Yiai!

sentences.zh: 」遂解衣顧監刑者曰：「亟斬我！

translations.literal: " He then stripped and told the supervising executioner: "Cut me down quickly!
translations.idiomatic: " He bared himself and told the executioner, "Strike quickly!

sentences.zh: 」斬之不殊，叱曰：「胡不力！

translations.literal: " The first stroke did not sever him; he shouted: "Why so weak!
translations.idiomatic: " The first stroke failed to kill him; he shouted, "Strike harder!

sentences.zh: 」三斬乃絕。

translations.literal: " Only on the third stroke did he die.
translations.idiomatic: " Only the third stroke ended him.

sentences.zh: 弟 萬淑萬淑亦以戰功顯。

translations.literal: Younger brother Wanshu — Wanshu also distinguished himself in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Wanshu — Wanshu also won distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 曆右領軍將軍、梁郡公、暢武道行軍總管。

translations.literal: He served through Right Commander of the Palace Guards, Duke of Liang commandery, and campaign commander of the Changwu Route.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Commander of the Palace Guards, Duke of Liang, and campaign commander on the Changwu route.

sentences.zh: 弟 萬備萬備有至行，居母喪，廬墓前，太宗詔表異其門。

translations.literal: Younger brother Wanbei — Wanbei had utmost conduct; dwelling in mourning for his mother he built a hut before the tomb; Taizong ordered his gate specially marked in commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Wanbei — Wanbei was a man of supreme filial conduct; mourning his mother he built a hut before her tomb, and Taizong ordered his gate specially honored.

sentences.zh: 以尚輦奉禦從伐高麗。

translations.literal: He followed as Director of the Imperial Carriage in the campaign against Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the campaign against Goguryeo as Director of the Imperial Carriage.

sentences.zh: 李勣圍白岩，虜遣兵萬餘來援，將軍契苾何力以八百騎苦戰，中槊創甚，為賊所窘，萬備單馬進救，何力獲免。

translations.literal: When Li Ji besieged Baiyan, the barbarians sent more than ten thousand to reinforce; General Qibi Heli fought bitterly with eight hundred horsemen, was severely wounded by a spear and trapped by the enemy; Wanbei rode in alone to rescue him and Heli escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ji besieged Baiyan, more than ten thousand enemy troops came to relieve the city; General Qibi Heli fought hard with eight hundred horsemen, was badly wounded by a spear and surrounded; Wanbei rode in alone and rescued him.

sentences.zh: 仕至左衛將軍。

translations.literal: He rose to Left Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Guard General.

sentences.zh: 在武德、貞觀時，又有盛彥師、盧祖尚、劉世讓、劉蘭、李君羨等，頗以功力顯，而皆不終，附于左。

translations.literal: In the Wude and Zhenguan eras there were also Sheng Yanshi, Lu Zushang, Liu Shirang, Liu Lan, Li Junxian, and others who showed themselves by martial achievement yet did not end well — appended at left.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude and Zhenguan periods Sheng Yanshi, Lu Zushang, Liu Shirang, Liu Lan, Li Junxian, and others also won notice through martial service yet came to bad ends — they are appended below.

sentences.zh: 附 盛彥師盛彥師者，宋州虞城人。

translations.literal: Appended: Sheng Yanshi — Sheng Yanshi was a man of Yucheng in Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Appended: Sheng Yanshi — Sheng Yanshi was from Yucheng in Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少任俠。

translations.literal: In youth he was given to chivalry.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was a man of chivalry.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，為澄城長。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye in Sui he was magistrate of Chengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui he was magistrate of Chengcheng.

sentences.zh: 高祖兵至汾陰，彥師率賓客上謁，授行軍總管，從平京師，與史萬寶鎮宜陽。

translations.literal: When Gaozu's army reached Fenyin, Yanshi led his retainers to present themselves and was appointed campaign commander; he followed in pacifying the capital and with Shi Wanbao garrisoned Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu's army reached Fenyin, Yanshi led his clients to submit and was made campaign commander; he helped pacify the capital and with Shi Wanbao garrisoned Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 李密叛，謀出山南，萬寶懼，謂彥師曰：「密，驍賊也，以王伯當輔之，挾思東歸之士，非計出萬全不為也，殆不可當。

translations.literal: Li Mi rebelled and planned to break out toward the southern mountains; Wanbao was afraid and said to Yanshi: "Mi is a fierce bandit, with Wang Bodang assisting him and carrying men who long to return east — unless the plan is absolutely secure he will not act; he can scarcely be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi rebelled and planned to break southward, Wanbao was afraid and told Yanshi, "Mi is a formidable rebel, aided by Wang Bodang and leading men who yearn to return east — he will not move without a plan he deems foolproof; he will be hard to stop.

sentences.zh: 」彥師笑曰：「請以數千兵為公梟其首。

translations.literal: " Yanshi laughed and said: "Allow me several thousand troops to take his head for you.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanshi laughed and said, "Give me a few thousand men and I will bring you his head.

sentences.zh: 」萬寶問計，答曰：「兵詭道也，難豫言。

translations.literal: " Wanbao asked the plan; he answered: "Warfare is the way of deception — it is hard to speak of beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: " Wanbao asked his plan; he replied, "War is deception — one cannot say in advance.

sentences.zh: 」即引眾逾洛水，入熊耳山，命士持滿夾道，伏短兵溪穀間，令曰：「賊半度乃擊。

translations.literal: " He immediately led the host across the Luo, entered Bear-Ear Mountain, ordered the men to hold full bows along the road, hid short weapons in streams and ravines, and commanded: "Strike when the bandits are half across.
translations.idiomatic: " He led his force across the Luo into Bear-Ear Mountain, posted archers with bows drawn along the path, hid short weapons in the streams and ravines, and ordered, "Attack when the enemy is half across."

sentences.zh: 」所部皆笑曰：「賊趨洛州，何為備此？

translations.literal: " All his subordinates laughed and said: "The bandits are heading for Luo Prefecture — why prepare this?"
translations.idiomatic: " His troops all laughed: "The rebels are bound for Luozhou — why set an ambush here?"

sentences.zh: 」彥師曰：「密聲言入洛，其實走襄城就張善相，我據其要，必禽之。

translations.literal: " Yanshi said: "Mi says aloud he is entering Luo, but in truth he will flee to Xiangcheng to join Zhang Shanxiang — I hold the choke point and shall surely capture him."
translations.idiomatic: " Yanshi said, "Mi proclaims he is entering Luoyang, but in truth he will flee to Xiangcheng to join Zhang Shanxiang; I hold the vital pass and will take him."

sentences.zh: 」密果至，彥師橫擊，首尾不相救，遂斬密及伯當。

translations.literal: " Mi indeed arrived; Yanshi struck across his line so head and tail could not aid each other, and beheaded Mi and Bodang.
translations.idiomatic: " Mi came as foretold; Yanshi struck across his column so van and rear could not support each other, and killed Mi and Wang Bodang.

sentences.zh: 以功封葛國公，授武衛將軍，鎮熊州。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Ge state, appointed Martial Guard General, and garrisoned Xiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was made Duke of Ge, appointed Martial Guard General, and posted to Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 討王世充也，彥師與萬寶軍伊闕，絕山南路。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Wang Shichong, Yanshi with Wanbao encamped at Yique and cut the southern mountain road.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Wang Shichong, Yanshi and Wanbao held Yique and severed the southern mountain route.

sentences.zh: 世充平，為宋州總管。

translations.literal: When Shichong was pacified, he became military governor of Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Shichong's fall he became military governor of Song.

sentences.zh: 始，彥師入關，世充以陳寶遇為宋州刺史，待其家不以禮。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yanshi entered the Pass, Shichong had made Chen Baoyu prefect of Song and did not treat his family with propriety.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanshi had first entered the Pass, Shichong had appointed Chen Baoyu prefect of Song and treated his family discourteously.

sentences.zh: 及是，彥師因事殺之，又殺平生所惡數十家，州人震駭，皆重足立。

translations.literal: Now Yanshi seized an occasion to kill him, and also killed several dozen households he had long hated; the people of the prefecture were shaken and walked as if on tiptoe.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yanshi used a pretext to kill him, and slaughtered several dozen families he had long hated; the prefecture was terrified, and men walked as if on coals.

sentences.zh: 徐圓朗反，詔為安撫大使，戰敗，為賊所執。

translations.literal: When Xu Yuanlang rebelled, an edict made him pacification commissioner; he was defeated and captured by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Yuanlang rebelled, he was named pacification commissioner, was defeated, and taken by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 圓朗待之厚，命作書招其弟，使舉虞城叛。

translations.literal: Yuanlang treated him generously and ordered him to write summoning his younger brother to raise Yucheng in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlang treated him well and ordered him to write urging his brother to rebel at Yucheng.

sentences.zh: 彥師為書曰：「吾奉使無狀，為賊禽，誓死報國。

translations.literal: Yanshi wrote: "I failed in my mission and was captured by bandits; I swear to repay the state with my death.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi wrote, "I failed in my charge and was taken by rebels; I swear to die for the state.

sentences.zh: 若宜善侍毋，勿以我為念。

translations.literal: If it is fitting, treat our mother well and do not think of me.
translations.idiomatic: If you can, care for our mother and do not grieve for me.

sentences.zh: 」圓朗笑曰：「將軍，壯士也。

translations.literal: " Yuanlang laughed and said: "General, you are a true stalwart.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanlang laughed and said, "General, you are a man of iron.

sentences.zh: 」置之。

translations.literal: " He let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: " He set the letter aside.

sentences.zh: 武德六年，圓朗平，彥師得還。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wude Yuanlang was pacified and Yanshi returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Wude (623) Yuanlang was suppressed and Yanshi returned.

sentences.zh: 高祖以罪誅之。

translations.literal: Gaozu executed him for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu executed him for his offenses.

sentences.zh: 附 盧祖尚盧祖尚，字季良，光州樂安人。

translations.literal: Appended: Lu Zushang — Lu Zushang, style Jiliang, was a man of Le'an in Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Appended: Lu Zushang — Lu Zushang, courtesy name Jiliang, was from Le'an in Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 家饒財，好施，以俠聞。

translations.literal: His family was wealthy and generous; he was known for chivalry.
translations.idiomatic: His family was rich and open-handed; he was known as a man of chivalry.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，募壯士捕盜，時年十九，善禦眾，所向有功，盜畏，不入境。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye in Sui he recruited stalwarts to hunt bandits; he was nineteen, skilled at controlling crowds, successful wherever he went; bandits feared him and did not enter his territory.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui he raised men to hunt bandits; at nineteen he was adept at commanding troops, won wherever he fought, and bandits dared not enter his district.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之亂，據州稱刺史，歃血誓眾，士皆感泣。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Yuwen Huaji he seized the prefecture and styled himself prefect, swore blood with the masses, and the warriors all wept.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuwen Huaji's rebellion he seized his prefecture, declared himself prefect, swore blood-oaths with his followers, and the men wept with emotion.

sentences.zh: 越王侗立，遣使歸地，因署本州總管，封沈國公。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yue Tong was established, he sent envoys to return the territory and was appointed military governor of his prefecture, enfeoffed Duke of Shen state.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yue was enthroned, he submitted his territory and was made military governor of his prefecture and Duke of Shen.

sentences.zh: 王世充僭位，以州歸高祖，授刺史，封弋陽郡公。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong usurped the throne, he returned the prefecture to Gaozu, was appointed prefect, and enfeoffed Duke of Yiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong seized the throne, he surrendered his prefecture to Gaozu, was made prefect, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 從趙郡王孝恭討輔公祏，為前軍總管，下宣、歙，進擊賊帥馮惠亮、陳正通，破之。

translations.literal: Following the Prince of Zhao Jun Xiaogong against Fu Gongshi, he was vanguard commander, took Xuan and She, advanced to strike the rebel leaders Feng Huiliang and Chen Zhengtong, and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: On the Prince of Zhao's campaign against Fu Gongshi he served as vanguard, took Xuan and She, advanced against Feng Huiliang and Chen Zhengtong, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 曆蔣州刺史、壽州都督、瀛州刺史，有能名。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Jiang, military governor of Shou, and prefect of Ying — everywhere he had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Jiang, military governor of Shou, and prefect of Ying, winning a name for competence everywhere he went.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，交州都督以賄敗，太宗方擇人任之，咸以祖尚才備文武，可用也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan the military governor of Jiaozhou fell for bribery; Taizong was selecting a replacement and all agreed Zushang had both civil and military talent and could be used.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenguan (628) the Jiaozhou governor was dismissed for bribery; Taizong sought a replacement, and all agreed Zushang combined civil and military gifts and was fit for the post.

sentences.zh: 召見內殿，謂曰：「交州去朝廷遠，前都督不稱職，公為我行，無以道遠辭也。

translations.literal: Summoned to the inner hall, Taizong said: "Jiaozhou is far from court; the former governor was incompetent — go for me; do not decline because the road is long."
translations.idiomatic: Called to the inner hall, Taizong told him, "Jiaozhou is remote and the last governor failed — go for me, and do not refuse because the journey is far."

sentences.zh: 」祖尚頓首奉詔，既而托疾自解，帝遣杜如晦等諭意曰：「匹夫不負然諾，公既許朕矣，豈得悔？

translations.literal: " Zushang kowtowed and accepted the edict; afterward he pleaded illness to withdraw; the Emperor sent Du Ruhui and others to explain: "A common man does not break his word — you have already promised me; how can you repent?
translations.idiomatic: " Zushang kowtowed and accepted; then he pleaded illness to back out; the emperor sent Du Ruhui and others to say, "Even a common man keeps his word — you have promised me; how can you withdraw?"

sentences.zh: 三年當召，不食吾言。

translations.literal: In three years I shall summon you — do not break my word to you.
translations.idiomatic: In three years I shall recall you — do not break faith with me.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「嶺南瘴癘，而臣不能飲，當無還理。

translations.literal: " He answered: "Lingnan has miasma, and I cannot drink — there will be no returning."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "The south is fever country, and I cannot drink wine — I shall not come back alive.

sentences.zh: 」遂固辭。

translations.literal: " He then firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: " He refused firmly.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「我使人不從，何以為天下！

translations.literal: The Emperor angrily said: "If I send a man and he will not obey, how can I rule the realm!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged: "If my orders are not obeyed, how can I govern the realm!

sentences.zh: 」命斬朝堂。

translations.literal: " He ordered execution in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered him beheaded in the hall.

sentences.zh: 既而悔之，詔復其官。

translations.literal: Soon he regretted it and an edict restored his office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon repented and restored his rank by edict.

sentences.zh: 附 劉世讓劉世讓，字元欽，京兆醴泉人。

translations.literal: Appended: Liu Shirang — Liu Shirang, style Yuanqin, was a man of Liquan in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Appended: Liu Shirang — Liu Shirang, courtesy name Yuanqin, was from Liquan in the capital district.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為徵仕郎。

translations.literal: In Sui he served as recruitment gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served as a recruitment gentleman.

sentences.zh: 高祖入長安，以湋川歸，授通議大夫。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered Chang'an, he submitted Weichuan and was appointed Grand Master for Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered Chang'an he submitted Weichuan and was made Grand Master for Discussion.

sentences.zh: 時唐弼餘黨寇扶風，世讓自請安輯，許之，得其眾數千，因授安定道行軍總管，率兵二萬拒薛舉，戰不勝，與弟寶皆沒於賊。

translations.literal: At the time remnants of Tang Bi's party raided Fufeng; Shirang volunteered to pacify them, was permitted, gathered several thousand of their followers, was then made campaign commander of the Anding Route, led twenty thousand troops to resist Xue Ju, was defeated, and he and his younger brother Bao were both taken by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Bi's remnants raided Fufeng, Shirang volunteered to pacify them, gathered several thousand men, was made campaign commander on the Anding route, led twenty thousand against Xue Ju, was defeated, and he and his brother Bao were captured.

sentences.zh: 舉令至城下，紿說使降。

translations.literal: Ju had him come beneath the walls and deceived him with talk of surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Ju brought him to the walls and feigned offers of surrender.

sentences.zh: 世讓陽許之，至則告守者曰：「賊兵極於此矣，善自固！

translations.literal: Shirang pretended to consent; on arrival he told the defenders: "The bandit host has reached its limit here — hold firm!
translations.idiomatic: Shirang feigned agreement; once inside he told the defenders, "The enemy has reached his limit here — hold fast!

sentences.zh: 」舉重其節，不加害。

translations.literal: " Ju respected his integrity and did not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: " Ju honored his steadfastness and did not harm him.

sentences.zh: 秦王方屯高墌，世讓密遣寶間走王，言賊虛實。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin was then encamped at Gaodi; Shirang secretly sent Bao to slip away to the Prince and report the enemy's condition.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin was at Gaodi; Shirang secretly sent Bao to reach the prince and report the enemy's strength.

sentences.zh: 高祖悅，賜其家帛千匹。

translations.literal: Gaozu was pleased and bestowed a thousand bolts of silk on his household.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was pleased and gave his family a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 舉平，授彭州刺史。

translations.literal: When Ju was pacified he was appointed prefect of Peng.
translations.idiomatic: When Ju fell he was appointed prefect of Peng.

sentences.zh: 俄領陝東道行軍總管，從永安王孝基討呂崇茂于夏縣，軍敗，為賊所囚。

translations.literal: Soon he also led the Shandong Route campaign command and followed Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji against Lü Chongmao at Xia county; the army was defeated and he was imprisoned by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he led the Shandong route army with Prince Yong'an Xiaoji against Lü Chongmao at Xia; the army was beaten and he was taken.

sentences.zh: 聞獨孤懷恩有逆謀，唐儉語世讓曰：「懷恩謀行，則國難未息，可亡歸，白髮之。

translations.literal: Hearing Dugu Huai'en harbored treason, Tang Jian said to Shirang: "If Huai'en acts, national peril will not cease — you can escape and report this to the white-haired one."
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Dugu Huai'en plotted treason, Tang Jian told him, "If Huai'en moves, the realm will not know peace — escape and warn the emperor."

sentences.zh: 」世讓逃還，高祖方濟河幸懷恩營，驚曰：「世讓之來，天也！

translations.literal: " Shirang fled back; Gaozu was crossing the river to visit Huai'en's camp and exclaimed: "Shirang's coming is Heaven's doing!
translations.idiomatic: " Shirang fled back as Gaozu was crossing the river toward Huai'en's camp; Gaozu cried, "Shirang's arrival is Heaven's work!

sentences.zh: 」因封為弘農郡公，賜田百畝、錢百萬。

translations.literal: " He was therefore enfeoffed Duke of Hongnong commandery and given a hundred mu of fields and a million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: " He was enfeoffed Duke of Hongnong and given a hundred mu of land and a million in cash.

sentences.zh: 母喪免，起為檢校并州總管。

translations.literal: Mourning for his mother removed him from office; he was recalled as acting military governor of Bing.
translations.idiomatic: He left office for his mother's mourning, then was recalled as acting military governor of Bing.

sentences.zh: 竇建德之援王世充也，世讓率萬騎出黃沙嶺，襲洛州。

translations.literal: When Dou Jiande came to aid Wang Shichong, Shirang led ten thousand horsemen out Huangsha Ridge to raid Luo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande aided Wang Shichong, Shirang led ten thousand horse out Huangsha Ridge to strike Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 會突厥入寇，又詔以兵屯雁門，世讓馳騎八百赴之，而可汗軍大至，乃保武州。

translations.literal: It happened the Turks invaded; another edict ordered him to garrison Yanmen; Shirang galloped eight hundred horse to the scene, but the khaghan's army came in great force and he therefore held Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks invaded he was ordered to Yanmen; Shirang raced eight hundred horsemen thither, but the khaghan came in force and he held Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 可汗與高開道、苑君璋合眾攻之，城數壞；

translations.literal: The khaghan with Gao Kaidao and Yuan Junzhang combined forces to attack; the walls were broken several times;
translations.idiomatic: The khaghan, Gao Kaidao, and Yuan Junzhang joined to attack; the walls were breached again and again;

sentences.zh: 輒立柵完拒。

translations.literal: each time he raised palisades to complete the defense and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: each time he threw up palisades and held them off.

sentences.zh: 鄭元璹先使可汗，可汗使來說，世讓叱曰：「丈夫奈何為夷狄作說客邪？

translations.literal: Zheng Yuansui had earlier been envoy to the khaghan; the khaghan sent someone to persuade him; Shirang shouted: "How can a man serve as a go-between for barbarians?
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuansui had been envoy to the khaghan, who now sent a persuader; Shirang thundered, "What man plays envoy for barbarians?

sentences.zh: 」久之，虜引去。

translations.literal: " After a long while the barbarians withdrew.
