translations.idiomatic: " In time the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 元璹還，具道其忠，賜良馬、金帶。

translations.literal: Yuansui returned and fully reported his loyalty; he was given fine horses and a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansui returned, reported his loyalty in full, and he received fine horses and a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 襄邑王神符鎮并州，世讓數以氣淩之，坐是削籍徙康州。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangyi Shenfu garrisoned Bing; Shirang repeatedly bullied him with his temper and for this was struck from the registers and banished to Kang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiangyi Shenfu held Bing; Shirang repeatedly browbeat him and was struck from the rolls and exiled to Kang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召授廣州總管。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned and appointed military governor of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as military governor of Guang.

sentences.zh: 帝問以備邊策，答曰：「突厥數南寇者，恃有馬邑為地耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked his border-defense strategy; he answered: "The Turks raid south repeatedly because they rely on Mayi as their ground.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his strategy for the frontier; he said, "The Turks raid south because they rely on Mayi as their base.

sentences.zh: 如使勇將屯崞城，厚儲金帛以招降者，數出奇兵略城下，踐禾稼，不逾歲，馬邑可圖也。

translations.literal: If brave generals garrison Zhuo city, store gold and silks lavishly to win defectors, and several times send picked troops to raid below the walls and trample the grain, within a year Mayi can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Post bold commanders at Zhuo, heap gold and silk to win defectors, and send raiders again and again to trample the crops below the walls — within a year Mayi can be seized."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「非公無可任者。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Apart from you there is no one fit for this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "No one but you can do this."

sentences.zh: 」乃使馳驛經略，於是世讓至馬邑。

translations.literal: " He then sent him post-haste to plan the matter; Shirang thereupon reached Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent him post-haste to carry out the plan; Shirang reached Mayi.

sentences.zh: 高滿政以地來降，突厥患之，縱反間，云：「世讓與可汗為亂。

translations.literal: Gao Manzheng submitted the territory in surrender; the Turks were troubled and spread counter-intelligence, saying: "Shirang is in league with the khaghan to raise trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Manzheng surrendered the region; the Turks spread slander that Shirang was plotting with the khaghan.

sentences.zh: 」帝不之察，因誅之，籍其家。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not investigate and therefore executed him and registered his household for confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not look into it and had him executed; his property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，突厥降者言世讓無逆謀，乃原其妻子。

translations.literal: In early Zhenguan surrendered Turks said Shirang had no treasonous plot; his wife and children were then pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan surrendered Turks said he had never plotted treason; his wife and children were spared.

sentences.zh: 附 劉蘭劉蘭字文郁，青州北海人。

translations.literal: Appended: Liu Lan — Liu Lan, style Wenyü, was a man of Beihai in Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Appended: Liu Lan — Liu Lan, courtesy name Wenyü, was from Beihai in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 仕隋鄱陽郡書佐。

translations.literal: In Sui he served as clerk of Poyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he was a clerk in Poyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 涉圖史，能言成敗事。

translations.literal: He studied histories and chronicles and could speak of success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: He studied histories and could discourse on rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 性陰狡，以天下將亂，見北海完富，潛介賊破其鄉，取子女玉帛。

translations.literal: By nature secretive and cunning, seeing the realm would fall into disorder and Beihai intact and wealthy, he secretly introduced bandits to break his district and took sons, daughters, jade, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Secretive and cunning, seeing chaos coming and Beihai still whole and rich, he secretly let bandits ravage his home district and seized women, jade, and silk.

sentences.zh: 淮安王神通安撫山東，率宗黨歸順。

translations.literal: Prince of Huai'an Shentong pacified Shandong; he led his clan to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai'an Shentong pacified Shandong; he led his lineage to submit.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，梁師都未平，蘭上書陳方略，太宗以為夏州都督府司馬。

translations.literal: In early Zhenguan, with Liang Shidu not yet pacified, Lan memorialized strategy; Taizong made him marshal of the Xia Prefecture command.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan, while Liang Shidu still held out, Lan submitted a plan; Taizong made him marshal of the Xia prefectural command.

sentences.zh: 師都以突厥兵頓城下，蘭僕旗息鼓，賊疑不敢迫，夜引去。

translations.literal: Shidu with Turk forces halted below the walls; Lan lowered banners and silenced drums; the enemy suspected and dared not press; at night they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shidu camped Turk troops below the walls; Lan hid his banners and stilled his drums; the enemy hesitated and dared not close; at night they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蘭追擊，破之，遂進軍夏州。

translations.literal: Lan pursued, defeated them, and advanced the army to Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lan pursued, broke them, and advanced on Xia.

sentences.zh: 師都平，遷豐州刺史，召為右領軍衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Shidu was pacified he was transferred to prefect of Feng and summoned as Right Commander of the Unicorn Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Shidu fell he was made prefect of Feng, then summoned as Right Commander of the Unicorn Guard.

sentences.zh: 十一年，為夏州都督長史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was chief administrator of Xia military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (637) he was chief administrator of Xia.

sentences.zh: 時突厥攜貳，郁射設阿史那摸末率屬帳居河南，蘭縱反間離之，頡利果疑。

translations.literal: At the time the Turks were divided; Yushishe Ashina Momo led dependent tents to dwell south of the river; Lan sowed dissension and Jieli indeed grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks were then divided; Yushishe Ashina Momo led dependent tents to settle south of the river; Lan sowed discord until Jieli grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 摸末懼，來降，頡利急追，蘭逆拒，卻其眾。

translations.literal: Momo feared and came to surrender; Jieli pursued hotly; Lan met and blocked him and drove off his host.
translations.idiomatic: Momo, afraid, surrendered; Jieli pursued hard; Lan met him and drove his force back.

sentences.zh: 封平原郡公，俄檢校代州都督。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan commandery and soon made acting military governor of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan and soon acting military governor of Dai.

sentences.zh: 初，長社許絢解讖記，謂蘭曰：「天下有長年者，咸言劉將軍當為天下主。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xu Xuan of Changshe explained prophecy books and told Lan: "There is a long-lived man in the realm who all say General Liu will become ruler under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xu Xuan of Changshe interpreted prophecy and told Lan, "Men say there is one who will live long as ruler — all say General Liu is destined for the throne."

sentences.zh: 」蘭子昭又曰：「讖言海北出天子，吾家北海也。

translations.literal: " Lan's son Zhao also said: "The prophecy says a Son of Heaven will come forth north of the sea — our family is from Beihai."
translations.idiomatic: " His son Zhao added, "The prophecy says the Son of Heaven will rise north of the sea — our house is Beihai."

sentences.zh: 」會鄠縣尉游文芝以罪繫獄當死，因發其謀，蘭及黨與皆伏誅。

translations.literal: " It happened the county lieutenant You Wenzhi, imprisoned for a capital crime, exposed the plot; Lan and his confederates were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: " The county lieutenant You Wenzhi, facing death in prison, exposed the plot; Lan and his party were all executed.

sentences.zh: 附 李君羨李君羨，洛州武安人。

translations.literal: Appended: Li Junxian — Li Junxian was a man of Wu'an in Luo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Appended: Li Junxian — Li Junxian was from Wu'an in Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 初事李密，後為王世充驃騎。

translations.literal: He first served Li Mi, later became Rapid Cavalry under Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Li Mi, then became Rapid Cavalry general under Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 惡世充為人，率其屬歸高祖，授上輕車都尉。

translations.literal: He detested Shichong's character, led his followers to Gaozu, and was appointed Colonel of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Disgusted with Shichong, he led his men to Gaozu and was made Colonel of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 秦王引置左右，從破宋金剛於介休，加驃騎將軍，賜以宮人、繒帛。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin placed him in his personal guard; following the defeat of Song Jingang at Jiexiu he was made Rapid Cavalry General and given palace women and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin kept him at his side; after the victory over Song Jingang at Jiexiu he was made Rapid Cavalry General and given palace women and silks.

sentences.zh: 從討王世充，為馬軍副總管。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Wang Shichong he was deputy commander of the horse army.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Shichong he was deputy commander of the horse army.

sentences.zh: 世充子玄應自武牢轉糧入洛，君羨俘其軍，玄應走。

translations.literal: Shichong's son Xuanying was moving grain from Wulao into Luoyang; Junxian captured his force and Xuanying fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong's son Xuanying was convoying grain from Wulao to Luoyang; Junxian seized the convoy and Xuanying fled.

sentences.zh: 從破竇建德、劉黑闥，所向必先登摧其鋒，累授左衛府中郎將。

translations.literal: Following the defeats of Dou Jiande and Liu Heita, wherever he went he was first to scale and break the enemy van; he was repeatedly made commandant in the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On campaigns against Dou Jiande and Liu Heita he was always first to storm the enemy line; he rose to commandant in the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 突厥至渭橋，君羨與尉遲敬德擊破之。

translations.literal: When the Turks reached the Wei Bridge, Junxian with Yuchi Jingde routed them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks reached the Wei Bridge, he and Yuchi Jingde drove them off.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「使皆如君羨者，虜何足憂！

translations.literal: Taizong said: "If all were like Junxian, what worry would there be of barbarians!
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "If all my officers were like Junxian, the barbarians would be nothing to fear!

sentences.zh: 」改左武候中郎將，封武連縣公，北門長上。

translations.literal: " He was made commandant of the Left Martial Guard, enfeoffed Duke of Wulian county, and senior commander at the northern gate.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made commandant of the Left Martial Guard, enfeoffed Duke of Wulian, and senior commander at the northern gate.

sentences.zh: 在仗讀書不休，帝嘉勞。

translations.literal: On guard duty he read without cease; the Emperor praised and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: On duty he read without pause; the emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 曆蘭州都督、左監門衛將軍。

translations.literal: He served as military governor of Lan and Left Director of the Gate Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He served as military governor of Lan and director of the Left Gate Guards.

sentences.zh: 先是，貞觀初，太白數晝見，太史占曰：「女主昌。

translations.literal: Earlier, in early Zhenguan, Venus repeatedly appeared by day; the grand astrologer divined: "The female principle will flourish."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in early Zhenguan, Venus had repeatedly appeared by day; the court astrologer read, "A woman will rise."

sentences.zh: 」又謠言「當有女武王者」。

translations.literal: " There was also a rumor that "a woman warrior-king will appear."
translations.idiomatic: " A rumor spread that "a woman warrior-king will come."

sentences.zh: 會內宴，為酒令，各言小字，君羨自陳曰「五娘子」。

translations.literal: At an inner feast they played a drinking game naming childhood names; Junxian declared himself "Fifth Daughter."
translations.idiomatic: At a palace feast a drinking game required childhood names; Junxian gave his as "Fifth Daughter."

sentences.zh: 帝愕然，因笑曰：「何物女子，乃此健邪！

translations.literal: The Emperor started and then laughed: "What sort of woman are you, to be so hardy!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started, then laughed: "What kind of woman are you, to be so bold!

sentences.zh: 」又君羨官邑屬縣皆「武」也，忌之。

translations.literal: " Moreover Junxian's offices and fiefs all bore the character Wu — the Emperor grew wary.
translations.idiomatic: " Moreover his posts and fiefs all contained the character wu (martial) — the emperor grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out as prefect of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 會御史劾奏君羨與狂人為妖言，謀不軌，下詔誅之。

translations.literal: It happened the censor impeached Junxian for demonic talk with madmen and plotting rebellion; an edict ordered his execution.
translations.idiomatic: The censor impeached him for sorcerous talk with madmen and plotting rebellion; an edict ordered his death.

sentences.zh: 天授中，家屬詣闕訴冤，武后亦欲自詫，詔復其官爵，以禮改葬。

translations.literal: In the Tianshou era his family came to court to plead injustice; Empress Wu also wished to display her magnanimity; an edict restored his office and rank and he was reburied with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianshou period his kin petitioned at court; Empress Wu wished to show her grace; an edict restored his rank and he was reburied with honor.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：侯君集位將相私謁太子，張亮養子五百人，薛萬徹與狂豎謀，皆死有餘責，又何咎哉？

translations.literal: Commentary says: Hou Junji in ministerial rank privately visited the crown prince; Zhang Liang raised five hundred foster sons; Xue Wanche plotted with madmen — all died with guilt to spare; what fault could there be?
translations.idiomatic: The commentators observe: Hou Junji, though he stood at the summit of power, paid secret court to the crown prince; Zhang Liang reared five hundred foster sons; Xue Wanche conspired with reckless men — each deserved death many times over; who could call their punishments unjust?

sentences.zh: 乙太宗之明德，蔽於謠讖，濫君羨之誅，徒使孽後引以自神，顧不哀哉！

translations.literal: With Taizong's bright virtue, he was blinded by rumors and prophecies, executed Junxian without cause, and only enabled the wicked posterity to cite it for self-divinization — how pitiful!
translations.idiomatic: Yet even Taizong's luminous virtue could be obscured by rumor and prophecy; he put Li Junxian to death on slight grounds, and only handed a later age of usurpers a tale to claim divine sanction — is that not lamentable?
